# ============================================================================
# Radancy / TalentBrew career-site hosts.
#
# Unlike the other files in this directory, every line here was probed live by
# this project on 2026-07-28 from a container that reaches job boards. Nothing
# below is an upstream annotation and nothing below is a guess: each host was
# asked for one page of
#
#   GET https://{host}{prefix}/search-jobs/results
#       ?CurrentPage=1&RecordsPerPage=1&SearchResultsModuleName=Search+Results
#
# and classified on what came back. The counts are that response's own
# data-total-job-results.
#
# The sections below are therefore not "verified" versus "unverified". They are
# verified-and-registered, verified-but-blocked-on-a-decision, and
# measured-not-to-be-Radancy. Read the section header before promoting anything.
#
# Format: one `company,host[,pathPrefix]` key per line, matching the key format
# internal/services/radancy.go parses (# = comment, inline OK). The pathPrefix
# is a per-tenant locale segment and is part of the endpoint, not decoration:
# jobs.veolia.com/search-jobs/results answers HTTP 301 and only
# jobs.veolia.com/fr/search-jobs/results answers with the board.
#
# Promotion rule, gated on content and not on status code: a Radancy response
# renders its results section with a data-total-job-results attribute even when
# the count is 0 (measured on www.att.jobs with a nonsense keyword), so the
# attribute's presence is the platform test and its value is the liveness test.
# Keep a host whose count is above zero.
# ============================================================================

# --- LIVE, and measured to be a near-mirror of a route already registered.
#     Staged rather than registered: promoting it means DELETING the other
#     route, which is a coverage decision with a real cost.
#
#     Tenet Healthcare publishes 3,350 postings here and 2,856 on Oracle Cloud
#     (tenet,eodr.fa.us2.oraclecloud.com,CX_1). Zero shared URLs, so
#     internal.Dedupe collapses nothing, and 1,818 shared title+location pairs --
#     85% of the Oracle board. The facility mix is the same on both to within a
#     percent (San Antonio 342 against 345, West Palm Beach 233 against 237, El
#     Paso 208 against 207). Radancy is the larger board and much the cheaper
#     one (4 requests against roughly 15), so it is the better route; it is
#     staged only because deleting the Oracle one is not this change's call.
#
#     Register it as "tenet" and not "tenethealth" when it is promoted. The
#     host-derived name does not collide with the "tenet" already registered, so
#     TestNoUnreviewedDoubleCountedEmployer would pass by not noticing, and this
#     overlap would enter the registry unreviewed.
#
#     METHOD NOTE, because it changes the answer. Comparing title+location pairs
#     verbatim gives ZERO overlap for this pair and would have read as two
#     disjoint boards. That is a formatting artifact: Oracle writes "San
#     Antonio, TX, United States" where Radancy writes "San Antonio, TX", so not
#     one of the 88 Radancy location strings equals any of Oracle's 114. The
#     1,818 above is after stripping the country suffix and expanding state
#     names. Any pair comparison across two platforms needs that normalisation
#     first or it will report every overlap as disjoint.
# tenet,jobs.tenethealth.com                     # 3350

# --- LIVE, but each collides with a company name already in the registry on a
#     different platform, and internal/services/double_count_test.go requires a
#     measured verdict before a colliding name may be registered. These are
#     staged rather than registered because the comparison has not been run, not
#     because there is any doubt they work. Crawl both boards, compare URLs
#     first and then normalised title+location pairs, add a reviewedDoubleCounts
#     row, then promote. ---
# baxter,jobs.baxter.com,/en                     # 541  -- also workday baxter.wd1
# bd,jobs.bd.com,/en                             # 987  -- Becton Dickinson; also oraclecloud bdousacampus + bdousaexperienced
# northwesternmedicine,jobs.nm.org               # 1386 -- also smartrecruiters northwesternmedicine
# pge,jobs.pge.com                               # 118  -- also successfactors pge,C0000161245P
#
# Checked and NOT a collision, recorded so it is not re-checked: careers.aldi.us
# (ALDI US, 1,213) against successfactors aldihofer,HoferSELive (Hofer, 230)
# shares zero URLs and zero titles. Different national businesses, and the names
# do not collide either, so no reviewedDoubleCounts row is required.

# --- LIVE, and DELIBERATELY NOT PROMOTABLE: each is the same board as a
#     registered host under a different locale, serving the identical posting
#     count. Radancy publishes one board per brand and routes locales by path
#     prefix, so registering two of these is not extra coverage, it is the same
#     employer crawled twice. The counts below are what made that visible. ---
# disney,emplois.disneycareers.com               # 800 -- same board as jobs.disneycareers.com
# disney,www.disneycareers.com,/en               # 800 -- same board as jobs.disneycareers.com
# veolia,jobs.veolia.com,/en                     # 2962 -- same board as veolia,jobs.veolia.com,/fr

# --- Radancy-shaped but answered HTTP 403 to this project's User-Agent, from
#     this container's IP, on both /search-jobs and /search-jobs/results. Each
#     kept the /search-jobs path rather than redirecting away from it, which is
#     what a non-Radancy host does, so these are probably real tenants behind a
#     bot wall rather than misattributions. A 403 is not evidence of a dead
#     board and it is not evidence of a live one either: registering these would
#     add permanently failing sources. Re-probe from CI, which has a different
#     egress, before promoting any of them.
#     Note lowes is separately uninteresting: it is already registered on both
#     phenom and workday and reviewedDoubleCounts calls that a sameEmployer
#     duplicate, so a third route would make it a triple. ---
# lowes,jobs.lowes.com                           # HTTP 403
# dominos,jobs.dominos.com                       # HTTP 403
# mcdonalds,careers.mcdonalds.com                # HTTP 403
# leidos,careers.leidos.com                      # HTTP 403
# centene,jobs.centene.com                       # HTTP 403
# natwest,jobs.natwestgroup.com                  # HTTP 403
# hcahealthcare,careers.hcahealthcare.com        # HTTP 403
# collinsaerospace,jobs.collinsaerospace.com     # HTTP 403
# jnj,careers.jnj.com                            # HTTP 403
# caesars,jobs.caesars.com                       # HTTP 503

# --- measured NOT to be Radancy, recorded so the same hosts are not re-probed.
#     All of these serve /search-jobs and would pass a path-shape check; none
#     returns a Radancy results fragment. This is the reason the probe above
#     gates on data-total-job-results rather than on the URL looking right. ---
# jobs.nscorp.com          /search-jobs/results returns an HTML page, not JSON
# www.careers.zurich.com   same

# jobs.thyssenkrupp.com    /en/search-jobs is a different vendor's template
#
# Employers whose careers host redirects to a platform already covered here,
# checked because issue #18 or docs/source-backlog.md named them:
# jobs.raytheon.com   -> 301 to careers.rtx.com/global/en/raytheon (Phenom shape)
# jobs.ebayinc.com    -> 303 to /us/en (Phenom shape)
# jobs.kroger.com     -> www.krogerfamilycareers.com/en/sites/CX_2001 (Oracle
#                        Recruiting Cloud, exactly as docs/source-backlog.md
#                        already records; do not re-add Kroger to Radancy)
# jobs.albertsons.com -> eofd.fa.us6.oraclecloud.com (Oracle Recruiting Cloud)
# jobs.dell.com       -> iawmqy.fa.ocs.oraclecloud.com (Oracle Recruiting Cloud)
# jobs.jpmorganchase.com -> jpmc.fa.oraclecloud.com (Oracle Recruiting Cloud)
# jobs.heidelbergmaterials.com -> heidelbergmaterials.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com
#
# ============================================================================
# How this list was built, and what it is not
#
# There is no directory of Radancy tenants to harvest. Radancy sites are served
# from the employer's own domain with no shared suffix, which is exactly why the
# key here is a full host: nothing about "www.att.jobs" or "careers.aldi.us" is
# derivable from the company name. This list is therefore a sweep of ~300
# plausible career hostnames, not an enumeration, and it is certainly a small
# fraction of the platform. The four brands docs/research/ats-platform-survey.md
# names (veolia, vinci, disneycareers, munichre) are all here and all live,
# which is the survey's endpoint template holding up; everything else was found
# by guessing hostnames and checking.
#
# The cheap way to extend it is a Common Crawl sweep for pages loading
# tbcdn.talentbrew.com or cdn.radancy.eu, which is the fingerprint every tenant
# measured carries. That was not available from this container.
# ============================================================================
